business_problem: UNDP needed more granular, forward-looking analytics to help governments and development partners decide where clean-energy investments would produce the greatest equity, development, and climate-resilience impact.
solution_summary: UNDP and IBM co-developed two public analytical tools to improve energy-planning decisions: the Clean Energy Equity Index and the Electricity Access Forecasting model. The first combines clean-energy potential, socioeconomic need, infrastructure readiness, and climate-risk indicators into a geospatial index that users can adjust through a dashboard to evaluate trade-offs across Africa. The second uses IBM watsonx.ai, IBM Cloud, IBM Environmental Intelligence data, and open-source machine-learning models to forecast electricity access through 2030 at one-kilometer resolution. Geospatial, demographic, infrastructure, land-use, and climate data are fused so policymakers can move beyond historical access maps and model future access gaps under different scenarios. UNDP teams use the dashboards to compare underserved populations, explore investment options, and align clean-energy strategies with broader development outcomes rather than relying on coarse national-level statistics.

solution_components.name: IBM watsonx.ai
solution_components.role: Runs the forecasting-model development used to project electricity access under future scenarios.

solution_components.name: IBM Cloud
solution_components.role: Hosts the analytical environment behind UNDP's public energy-planning models and dashboards.

solution_components.name: IBM Environmental Intelligence
solution_components.role: Provides environmental and climate data used by the forecasting and equity models.

data_flow: Geospatial, demographic, infrastructure, land-use, energy-potential, and climate-risk data are combined into the Clean Energy Equity Index and Electricity Access Forecasting model, where watsonx.ai and open-source ML generate country-level forecasts and scorecards that are surfaced through dashboards for policymakers and financing partners.
business_outcome: UNDP strengthened its ability to support equitable energy planning, gave governments scenario-based visibility into underserved populations and investment trade-offs, and expanded the geographic reach of its analytics across Africa and the broader Global South.
